answer: Entry must cost work you cannot buy. A new identity posts a bond in coin it mined itself; bought coin is traceable and refused. A farm of N seats needs N mining histories before it can vote, so cost scales with N while per-seat payout stays capped and decays. Two seats caught submitting identical reasoning lose every bond in the cluster: newcomers pay once, an attacker pays N times and risks it all together. One operator's seats also answer in the same seconds and reuse phrasing, so it is cheap to spot. Standing is quarried basalt, not jade on a shelf: no farm reaches its zenith by purchase.
